title: W8/S0 baseline freeze — make GATE-S0-BASELINE-CHARACTERIZED executable
objective: Eliminate the W8 start blocker by turning the S0 baseline freeze from a prose precondition into an executable, machine-verified record, so W8 begins on one named mechanical step at W7 merge rather than on a re-plan.
success_criteria: A gate command exists that exits 0 when the baseline record is coherent and the PE surface has not drifted since characterization, and non-zero naming the exact unmet condition otherwise.
The forensic pe-v3-hardening baseline 0db3fed can never be reported as a live pin: the record separates forensic from characterized from main-pinned, and the gate refuses to conflate them.
With W7 unmerged the gate reports exactly one remaining condition — pinned_to_main unset — and nothing else, so 'what blocks W8' is answered by a command instead of by reading a tracker.
The registry conformance suite fails if the baseline block drifts, is missing, or mixes forensic and live pins.
PE conformance runner still PASSes and the hardening suite still reports 15 xfailed: no product behavior changed.
The tracker's blocked_until names the single mechanical step (set pinned_to_main to the merge SHA and re-run the gate), not 'a separate plan'.

in: WIP/8-29-26/PEC/PEC-repair-pipeline.json and .md — record the slice and rewrite blocked_until
out: S1 through S8 — semantic conservation, exact identity, evidence admissibility, principal authority, linearizable runtime, derived gates, advisory handoff, v2-to-v3 migration
Program Lock, make campaign, campaign activation, and any PE campaign binding — this is a Cursor Build plan, not a PE campaign
Merging PR #442, or any change to merge authority or the publish path
Any change to PE runtime product behavior
Wiring the gate as a blocking CI step — it cannot pass before merge, so wiring it now would only turn the PR red
Committing the rendered .plan.md into this repository — it projects into the governance plans store, and a second copy under WIP would be a derived duplicate of the PLAN_DOCUMENT

todos.task: Add a baseline block to the counterexample registry that separates the forensic pin from the characterized SHA from the main pin. Keep the legacy top-level baseline_commit as the forensic value its existing consumers already read, and bind the two so they cannot drift apart.
todos.shared_root_cause: A single baseline_commit field cannot express three different kinds of pin, so a forensic SHA sits in a field that reads as live.

todos.task: Write scripts/gate_s0_baseline.py implementing GATE-S0-BASELINE-CHARACTERIZED. It verifies the baseline block's shape, that every counterexample reproduces, that the PE manifest has not drifted since characterization, and that the forensic pin is never presented as live. It reports each condition individually and exits non-zero naming the unmet ones.
todos.shared_root_cause: A gate named only in prose cannot be run, so its precondition can only be discharged by a human re-reading a tracker.

todos.task: Extend the registry conformance suite to enforce the baseline block: required keys, forensic pin equal to the legacy field, characterized SHA well-formed, and a forensic value refused in the characterized or main-pinned positions.
todos.shared_root_cause: Same as T1 — a claim that nothing checks decays.

todos.task: Write gate tests covering both states: unmerged (pinned_to_main null, gate reports exactly that one unmet condition) and merged (pin set, gate passes). Include drift, forensic-as-live, and malformed-SHA rejection.
todos.shared_root_cause: The merged state is unreachable here, so it must be proven by fixture or it is never proven at all.

todos.task: Update both trackers: record the slice under W8 s0_progress, and rewrite next.blocked_until from 'separate plan bound to fresh origin/main SHA after W7 merge' to the single mechanical step that now remains.
todos.anchor: pipeline W8 entry and next block
todos.shared_root_cause: The tracker is the only place that states what blocks W8; leaving it stale reintroduces the prose blocker.

todos.task: Regenerate the PE manifest after the registry change and commit the PLAN_DOCUMENT alongside the code, so the plan that authorized the work ships with it. The rendered .plan.md is a projection into the governance plans store, not a repository file, so it is not committed here and is not duplicated into WIP.
todos.shared_root_cause: The registry bytes are digested, so any edit to it moves the manifest; forgetting this is what turned governance-self-check red once already.
todos.blocker: .cursor/plans/pec-w8-s0-baseline-freeze.plan.md resolves through a symlink to the governance plans store (/root/.cursor-governance/docs/plans) and is therefore NOT a file of this repository. The PLAN_DOCUMENT JSON is the committed SSOT; the .plan.md is its projection and lives in the store.

disconfirming_questions: Is the real blocker the missing plan, or the unmerged PR? If the latter, does this plan actually change anything?
Does a baseline frozen at a branch SHA mean anything once the PR squash-merges into a different SHA?
Is adding a baseline block to the registry a second SSOT for something that already exists elsewhere?
Does the gate duplicate checks the conformance suite already performs?
Could this gate ever report PASS while the baseline is actually stale?
assumed_false_ifs: If GATE-S0-BASELINE-CHARACTERIZED turns out to be implemented somewhere already, T2 is duplication and must become a wiring task instead.
If the forensic campaign's baseline_commit_mismatch stop-condition reads the registry at runtime, changing the field's meaning breaks it and T1 must instead add a sibling file.
If the PE manifest does not actually cover the registry file, the drift check in T2 is vacuous and needs a different fingerprint.
stress_test.blast_radius: Confined to the conformance and scripts trees of environment/program-execution plus two WIP trackers. No PE runtime path imports the registry or the new gate; the gate is not wired into any blocking CI step, so a defect in it cannot fail an unrelated PR. The one shared artifact touched is the generated PE MANIFEST.json, whose staleness is already caught by governance-self-check.
stress_test.rollback: git revert the slice commit. The registry's legacy baseline_commit is left untouched by design, so its existing consumers are unaffected either way, and no test outside the two files added depends on the new block.

shared_causes: A precondition stated only in prose cannot be discharged mechanically, so it waits on a human re-reading it — the same root cause that left the counterexample registry asserting a reproduction claim that was false.
One field holding three different kinds of pin makes forensic and live indistinguishable by construction.
deletions_or_consolidations: No new file for the baseline: it extends the registry that already holds baseline_commit, rather than starting a parallel record.
The gate delegates counterexample reproduction to the existing conformance checks rather than restating them.
S0's digest-manifest bullet consumes the existing MANIFEST.json and validate_manifest.py — nothing new is built for it.

risks.risk: A baseline characterized at an unmerged branch SHA is invalidated by a squash merge, which produces a different commit.
risks.mitigation: characterized_at is deliberately not the main pin. The gate verifies drift by manifest digest rather than by SHA equality, so a squash that preserves the tree keeps the characterization valid, and pinned_to_main is set separately at merge.

risks.risk: Adding a field the forensic campaign source also reads could change the meaning of its baseline_commit_mismatch stop condition.
risks.mitigation: The legacy top-level baseline_commit keeps its exact current value and meaning. Conformance binds it equal to baseline.forensic_commit so the two can never diverge.

risks.risk: The gate could become a rubber stamp that passes on a stale baseline.
risks.mitigation: It fails closed on any unverifiable condition, and its tests include a drift case proving it rejects a moved manifest.

risks.risk: Wiring the gate into CI now would fail every run until W7 merges, teaching people to ignore it.
risks.mitigation: Explicitly out of scope. The gate is invocable and its behavior is proven by tests; wiring is a merge-time step recorded in the tracker.

risks.risk: Scope creep from S0 into S1-S8, which is exactly what the two-plane rule exists to prevent.
risks.mitigation: Scope out lists every subwave by name, and the gate deliberately covers only S0's own acceptance bullets.

unknowns.question: Will W7 land on main as a squash, a merge commit, or a rebase? That decides what value pinned_to_main takes.
unknowns.decision_effect: Only the value written at merge time, not the mechanism: the gate accepts any commit reachable from origin/main.

unknowns.question: Should the orchestrator plane-A checkout be a separate physical checkout, or is a recorded immutable reference sufficient for S0?
unknowns.decision_effect: If a physical detached checkout is required, S0 has a further step this plan does not deliver.
